questions.stem: Why do simple covalent substances not conduct electricity?

options.text: They have very strong covalent bonds
They have no free charged particles such as ions or delocalised electrons
They are always gases at room temperature
Their molecules are too small to carry a current

questions.explanation: Simple covalent substances do not conduct electricity because they have no free charged particles. Their molecules are electrically neutral (no ions), and all their electrons are used in covalent bonds (no delocalised electrons). Even when melted, they remain as neutral molecules.
